summary: Well-known SIP ports come from the RFCs and IANA. Cloud ranges below were read from the vendor page on the date in this file. If a vendor edits the page, the page wins.

rows.name: SIP
rows.purpose: Default port when a SIP URI has no port.
rows.note: DNS SRV can publish a different port. RFC 3263.

rows.name: SIP over TLS
rows.purpose: Default port for a SIPS URI.
rows.note: A trunk can listen elsewhere if DNS or the peer is explicit.

rows.name: STUN
rows.purpose: STUN binding and TURN allocation on the IANA stun port.
rows.note: TURN is specified in RFC 8656 and uses this port unless configured otherwise.

rows.name: STUN/TURN over TLS
rows.note: Also registered for STUN over TLS. See RFC 8489.

rows.name: DNS
rows.purpose: Name, NAPTR, and SRV lookups for SIP servers.
rows.note: Large answers fall over to TCP. RFC 1035.

rows.name: RTP
rows.purpose: Media port is in SDP. There is no single IANA RTP port.
rows.note: The usual convention is an even port. The SDP m= line is the authority. RFC 8866.

rows.name: RTCP
rows.purpose: Reports and feedback for the RTP stream.
rows.note: Without mux or an a=rtcp line, RTCP is the next higher port. RFC 3550.

rows.name: MSRP
rows.purpose: IANA default for Message Session Relay Protocol.
rows.note: Session setup is still SDP. The MSRP URI can carry another port.

rows.name: SIP over WebSocket
rows.purpose: WebSocket is a transport for SIP, usually on HTTP(S) ports.
rows.note: There is no dedicated IANA SIP-WebSocket port.

rows.name: NTP
rows.purpose: Clock sync. TLS certificates and some phones depend on it.
rows.note: Webex Calling also lists UDP 123 for devices. See the port reference.

rows.name: Teams Direct Routing signaling
rows.purpose: SIP/TLS from the certified SBC to the Teams SIP proxy.
rows.note: Read 2026-10-15. FQDNs: sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com, sip2, sip3. Return traffic uses the port configured on the SBC. Microsoft can change this page.

rows.name: Teams Direct Routing media
rows.purpose: Media between the SBC and Teams media processors.
rows.note: Read 2026-10-15. Allow the published IP ranges, not only the addresses a single DNS answer returned.

rows.name: Webex Calling signaling (registration trunk and devices)
rows.purpose: Outbound SIP-TLS to Webex Calling for registration-based trunks and devices.
rows.note: Page change log dated 2026-09-07 expands phone source ports to 5060-5280. Local Gateway source is listed as 8000-65535. The help page wins if Cisco edits it.

rows.name: Webex Calling signaling (certificate trunk)
rows.purpose: Outbound SIP-TLS for a certificate-based Local Gateway trunk.
rows.note: Inbound from Webex to a certificate-based gateway uses a customer-chosen destination port. Registration-based gateways reuse the outbound connection.

rows.name: Webex Calling media
rows.purpose: Destination ports the port reference lists for SRTP toward Webex Calling.
rows.note: Local Gateway source range on that page is UDP 8000-48199. Device source media is a narrower range (19560-19661 for many devices). Do not collapse those into one rule.

matrix.ports: 5060 unless the URI or SRV says otherwise
The m= port, plus RTCP on the next port unless mux or a=rtcp
3478 and 5349 unless the server URI differs

matrix.to: sip.pstnhub.microsoft.com and the sip2/sip3 failover names
matrix.ports: Destination 5061. Allow return traffic to the SBC signaling port.
3478-3481 and 49152-53247, both directions, plus the published IP ranges
Destination 8934. Device source 5060-5280 as of the 2026-09-07 note.
Destination 5062. Inbound to the gateway uses the customer port.

quiz.q: A SIP URI has no port. UDP is the transport. Which destination port do you try first?
quiz.why: 5060 is the default SIP port. 5061 is the SIPS default. DNS SRV can still override either one.

quiz.q: Which port is the default for a SIPS URI?
quiz.why: SIPS means TLS, and the default port is 5061.

quiz.q: Where does RTP learn its UDP port?
quiz.why: RTP has no single well-known port. The offer and the answer each name a port.

quiz.q: RTCP is not multiplexed and there is no a=rtcp line. RTP is on UDP 40000. Where is RTCP?
quiz.why: The classic rule is the next higher port. RFC 5761 mux puts both on the RTP port when negotiated.

quiz.q: Which IANA port do STUN binding requests use unless the server says otherwise?
quiz.why: 3478 is stun. 5349 is the TLS port.

quiz.q: Teams Direct Routing signaling from a certified SBC uses which destination port?
quiz.why: Microsoft’s Direct Routing plan says SIP/TLS to the Teams proxy on 5061. Re-check that page before you build a firewall.

quiz.q: A Webex Calling registration-based trunk sends SIP-TLS to which destination port on the port reference?
quiz.why: The Webex Calling port reference lists 8934 for registration-based trunks and 5062 for certificate-based trunks.

quiz.q: Which document tells a SIP element how to turn a domain into a host and port?
quiz.why: RFC 3263 is the locating-SIP-servers document: NAPTR, SRV, then A or AAAA.
